reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a Pionex spot-futures arbitrage bot by presenting reported two-month earnings as passive income and directing viewers to register on Pionex. The registration request is materially tied to the displayed performance figures because the platform and bot are the subjects of those figures, rather than merely ordinary channel engagement. The video discloses that the figures are personal past results and are not guaranteed, and the records do not independently establish the platform's performance, viewer outcomes, required deposits, or any completed loss.

citations.quote: Pionex spot-futures arbitrage bot 2 month results. Register on Pionex here:
Pionex Spot-Futures Arbitrage Bot [ 2 Month Pionex Results ]
the profit after two months is $64
He's making me money he's making me a passive income
Are you happy with three percent a month

opening.argument: This presentation is framed with unusually direct risk disclosures, which undercuts a deceptive-returns characterization. It expressly says the information is opinion and informational, is not investment advice, and does not guarantee gains. It also identifies cryptocurrency as highly speculative and warns that past results do not guarantee future results. The speaker likewise says these are current personal earnings and repeats that past results are no guarantee for future results. A viewer is therefore given the central limitation needed to evaluate the reported outcome: it is one person’s historical experience, not a promise or certification of safety.

citations.quote: I am not guaranteeing you gains on your investment
Past results don't guarantee future results.
these are my current earnings. But always remember, past results are no guarantee for future results.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference argument treats the registration link and earnings discussion as enough to establish scam content, but it acknowledges that the video discloses personal past results and no guarantee. The quoted earnings statement describes what the presenter reports, not what viewers will receive. Nor does a link itself establish deception when the accompanying material expressly warns that gains are not guaranteed.

citations.quote: I can only show you my results so that you have a general idea.
I am not guaranteeing you gains on your investment

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Warnings do not erase the promotional thrust. The video still connects a named bot with reported earnings and asks viewers whether they would be happy with three percent a month. Saying the results are personal and uncertain limits liability, but it does not change the fact that the favorable performance is being used to attract interest in the platform.

opening.argument: The material can reasonably be understood as a hands-on demonstration and follow-up review of an automated trading tool. The speaker says he will show his two-month bot earnings, then walks through the results and explains that an arbitrage bot should be relatively safe and differs from a crypto trading bot. The sampled frames show the platform’s bot-results interface and transaction history rather than a vague promise detached from an observable tool. He also invites questions and comparisons from viewers, which is consistent with commentary about a technology and personal test rather than a concealed solicitation.

citations.quote: in this video I'm going to show you my two month BionX spot futures arbitrage bot earnings
An arbitrage bot should be pretty safe
this is an arbitrage bot so it's difficult to compare an arbitrage bot between a crypto. Trading bot

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling it a demonstration does not make the evidence a scam. The reference side identifies no guaranteed outcome, required deposit, or completed viewer transaction. Its own quoted material shows only a personal walkthrough of results. A platform link can accompany a review or demonstration without converting every discussion of performance into deceptive solicitation.

citations.quote: I can only show you my results so that you have a general idea.
if you have any questions also ask them in the comment section below

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The interface and walkthrough establish that the bot is being displayed, but they do not establish that the displayed figures are independently verified or representative. The speaker’s explanation that arbitrage should be safe and his question about three-percent monthly returns make the demonstration favorable, while the registration link gives viewers a path to act on that favorable presentation.

opening.argument: At most, this is ordinary promotion of access to a named trading service accompanied by a personal review. The description discloses that some links may generate a small affiliate commission at no additional cost, which makes the commercial relationship visible rather than hidden. Crucially, the record does not show a demand for a deposit, a credential request, a guaranteed return, a downline, or a completed loss. The speaker instead states that he is not guaranteeing gains and that past results do not predict the future. Those missing mechanisms matter: a referral link and historical performance claim alone do not prove a scam.

citations.quote: Some of these links are affiliate links where I'll earn a small commission if you make a purchase at no additional cost to you.
I am not guaranteeing you gains on your investment
past results are no guarantee for future results
Register on Pionex here:

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference side relies on the subject matter and referral link, but those establish neither a fraudulent mechanism nor a promised viewer return. It expressly concedes that the records do not establish deposits, transfers, guaranteed returns, or viewer losses. The affiliate disclosure further identifies the possible commercial incentive instead of concealing it, while the disclaimer rejects a guarantee.

citations.quote: Some of these links are affiliate links where I'll earn a small commission if you make a purchase at no additional cost to you.
I am not guaranteeing you gains on your investment

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A scam classification does not require proof that a viewer already lost money. The relevant combination is a referral path to the platform plus favorable claims that the bot produced passive income and roughly three percent monthly returns. The affiliate disclosure reveals compensation but does not make the promotion non-deceptive, and the missing deposit or loss evidence cannot turn favorable marketing into verified ordinary commerce.
